newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS REFUTE "WEAK" DESCRIPTION.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS REFUTE "WEAK" DESCRIPTION.

text.p: The British Lions rejected claims of weakness in their tight five after cruising to a 39-11 win over an Eastern Province Invitation XV on Saturday.
E.P. hooker and skipper Jaco Kirsten said South Africa should attack the touring side in the forwards, despite seeing his side concede five tries to one.

"We can take them up front. Scrum-wise and maybe in the lineouts they are vulnerable," said Kirsten. "We had them going at one time. I would say the physical strength of the tight five is a weakness."

Lions manager Fran Cotton rejected the idea. "We were playing a tough, big pack of forwards with a big South African front row and a couple of Antipodeans in the back row but I thought we did well against them. I wouldn't agree that we're vulnerable."

Kirsten was full of praise for the Lions backs however in which centres Jeremy Guscott (2) and Will Greenwood as well as replacement wing Tony Underwood all crossed for tries -- four of them in the last 18 minutes.
"The skills of the backline were exceptional," said Kirsten. "They way they worked as a unit was very good but we missed some important first time tackles."
Guscott, on his third Lions tour, said: "The best bits we produced were from what we have been doing in training but some of the mistakes were from a side that hasn't played together before.
"But we were definitely satisfied in the changing room afterwards."
Coach Ian McGeechan added: "I was delighted by the way we finished the game. I thought we had a very good first 20 minutes but we lost control of the game in the middle period.
"But what impressed me was the way we got back into the game and to finish so positively gives us a lead into what we want to do in the coming weeks.
"To score 39 points and concede only one try was very encouraging for us. I thought we defended well."
The Lions are next in action on Wednesday when they play Border in East London.
